title: Jesu, Delight of Every Heart
description: Jesu, Delight of Every Heart in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Latin hymns of the early Church for Hymns of the Early Church (London, 1896), headed “Jesu, Dulcedo Cordium”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-su, de-light of ev-ery heart, Thou font of life, Thou source of light, Earth can no joy so real im-part, No soul can form a hope so bright.

lines: Jesu, delight of every heart,
Thou font of life, Thou source of light,
Earth can no joy so real impart,
No soul can form a hope so bright.
Abide with us, O Lord, we pray,
And cause Thy heavenly light to glow;
Drive from our minds the clouds away,
And let the world Thy sweetness know.
When Thou dost seek the humble heart,
Thy heavenly truth is freely given;
Then vanities of earth depart,
Then glows the fervent love of heaven.
O Jesus, of Thy wondrous grace,
Make us Thy boundless love to know;
And when we see Thee face to face,
To us Thy matchless glory show.
They know how sweet the Lord can be,
Who deeply drink His love divine;
How blest, who find their all in Thee,
Nor thirst for other joys than Thine.
O Thou the spring whence pity flows!
Light from the Fatherland to cheer!
To us Thy glorious light disclose,
Nor let dark clouds afflict us here.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Early Church (1896)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Latin, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Early Church; set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
